style.summary:
style of A: A is directive and somewhat impatient, with repeated just and instructions such as just look at those distributions.
style of B: B is minimal and agreeable, answering with Yeah.

A: A's directive instructions make A the one who tells B what to do.
A's impatient repetition of just pushes B toward A's approach.
A's confident tone closes the question of how to read the plot.
B: B's agreeable Yeah lets B signal acceptance and withdraw it whenever B chooses.
B's minimal tone keeps B's own position undisclosed.
B's compliance is conditional, which leaves B able to resist later.

A: A's directions are shaped by the plot B made, so B's choice of display limits what A can instruct.
A's impatience is answered by B's brief Yeah, which means B's agreement is what closes each point.
A's confident tone can be challenged by B asking to revisit the plot, so the reading is not final.
B: B's Yeah is acknowledgement only, so B does not hold a real veto over the instructions.
B's plot is the referent because A describes it as You've plotted them here, which makes A the one who sets the topic.
B's withheld position gives B no stake, which leaves A free to decide.

content.summary:
content of A: A's content is about the plot, with three colours representing silence and the distributions.
content of B: B's content is minimal, only agreement with A's points.

A: A's identification of the three categories defines the content of the plot.
A's statement that the silence category is fine settles a substantive question.
A's direction to examine the distributions sets what the content should be about.
B: B's plotting of the data gives B the source material that the content is built on.
B's choice of display determines what can be examined in the content.
B's agreement with each point confirms the content as B's to shape.

A: A's categories depend on the plot B made, so B's choice determines the content.
A's claim about silence can be contested, so the substance is not settled by A.
A's direction is limited to what B's plot shows, so the content is B's.
B: B's plot is the material A refers to, so A is the one who gives the content meaning.
B's agreement adds no substance, so the content is A's.
B's display does not limit the substance A chooses to discuss.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A holds the floor and gives instructions, interrupting with just -.
coordination of B: B gives back-channels and does not take turns.

A: A holds the floor for most of the exchange, which shows A controls the sequence.
A's interruptions with just cut B off and keep the direction under A's control.
A's closing of each point shows A decides when the topic changes.
B: B's back-channels leave the floor open for B to take at any time.
B's agreement at each pause gives B the ability to close points.
B's refusal to take turns keeps B from being pushed into a position.

A: A's floor is given by B's back-channels, so B decides when A has the floor.
A's interruptions are answered by B's brief agreement, which means B closes the points.
A's closing is only a statement, so B's acceptance or rejection still decides the change.
B: B's back-channels do not take the floor, so B's option to take it is never used.
B's agreement does not close points that A keeps raising, so the control stays with A.
B's abstention from turns leaves A to choose the direction.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A is engaged in guiding the task, though directive.
engagement of B: B is passive, showing less engagement.

A: A's guiding of the task shows strong investment in the outcome.
A's directive stance keeps A at the centre of the task.
A's attention to the distributions shows A is engaged with the detail.
B: B's passivity keeps B's own interest private, which gives B room to decide later.
B's agreement shows B is following the task closely enough to respond.
B's low engagement allows B to withhold commitment until it matters.

A: A's guidance is active, but B's willingness to follow shapes whether the task moves forward.
A's central place depends on B's continued agreement, so B holds the outcome.
A's detail is what B plotted, so the engagement with the data is B's.
B: B's passivity leaves no stake in the outcome, so A's engagement is the one that matters.
B's agreement is shallow, so the following is not real involvement.
B's withheld commitment is never revealed, so A's direction stands.
